purpose: GT-only trajectory design, revision 2. Written after the v1 GT-only run and before any moved-state neural render.
revision_reason: v1 null-control candidates both failed the declared rule: T1a (milk pot -x 0.10) interpenetrates the tray rim (exact mesh distance 0); T1b (milk pot +z 0.15) keeps the pot-teapot gap near 0.17 but slides the pot's mirror image across the teapot, giving an interaction-ROI GT change of 0.062 display MAE, 94% of T3's 0.066. The tray rim bounds the milk pot, so no remote single-part move exists. The physical-signal gate passed in v1 (T2 5.6x, T3 8.8x repeat noise); approach states are unchanged.
camera_lighting: upstream scenes/teaset get_scene(res) defaults: camera theta=60 phi=160 r=2.5 target (0,0.2,0), fov 35; envmap textures/envmap.exr rotated 90 deg about y; reference integrator prb max_depth -1 rr_depth 5
mover: teapot2 (milk pot); translation along the flat tray floor only

state_notes.T1: Whole asset translated +z 0.15: every part moves as much as the milk pot does in T1b, all inter-part relations are preserved exactly; with distant envmap lighting the asset-frame transport is unchanged except for viewpoint parallax.
state_notes.T1b: Same milk-pot displacement vector as T1 with the other parts fixed: relation changes at nearly constant gap (0.172 vs 0.187).
state_notes.T3: Pot-teapot exact gap 0.034 (the canonical tin-teapot gap is 0.035).

null_control_rule: T1 qualifies as the low-interaction control if its surface-corresponded interaction-ROI GT change (display MAE vs T0, seed set A) is at most 25% of T3's. If it does not, the batch reports that no null control was found; no further null redesign.
